title: Scientists Find Missing Matter Hiding Around Galaxies
summary:
Scientists have long figured out how much matter should be in the universe. But more than half of the ordinary matter seemed to be missing. Now they think they know where some of it is hiding.

Ordinary matter is made of tiny particles, like the protons and neutrons in stars, planets and people. It is different from dark matter, a mystery stuff that does not give off light.

Haochen Wang, a student at the Massachusetts Institute of Technology, led the new study. He says the missing matter is a thin gas spread out in huge, faint clouds around galaxies. In some places, there is less than one tiny particle in a space the size of a washing machine!

To find it, the team used fast radio bursts. These are quick flashes of radio waves from far away. When a burst passes through gas, its signal gets stretched out. More gas means more stretching.

Not everyone agrees this is the first discovery. But astronomer Vikram Ravi called it "a great signpost of what is to come."
why_it_matters: Finding missing matter helps us understand what everything in the universe, including you, is made of.
